description:
The two readers disagree about malformed keys under `s/{shard_tag}/`.

`Snapshot.read_latest/1` takes the first listed key with no fallback and no validation. Because keys are inverted versions sorted newest-first, a junk name that happens to sort ahead of the real bundles is selected -- and then fails. One stray file makes the newest snapshot unreachable.

`Snapshot.list/2` silently drops names it cannot parse. So retention logic counts a prefix it cannot fully see, and may make decisions (including pruning) against an inaccurate view of what is actually stored.

Two problems from one inconsistency: the same malformed object is fatal to one reader and invisible to the other. Neither reports it.

Given that a corrupt snapshot is already fatal to cold start (see sibling ticket), 'one stray file in the bucket' is a bigger blast radius than it should be.

Partly anticipated by bedrock-q67.21.19 (unparseable keys are errors). Found while building bedrock-hve.3, which now reports these offline as :unparsable_snapshot_key / :malformed_snapshot_key.
title: [BUG] Snapshot.read_latest/1 bricks on one unparsable bundle name while Snapshot.list/2 silently drops it
